305: Blood-C by CLAMP (Dark Horse), with art by Ranmaru Kotone, is a dark supernatural horror story with plenty of action. Saya Kisaragi is a cheerful, clumsy high school girl in a quiet country town, but by night she serves as a shrine maiden, taking up a sword to fight the Elder Bairns, monsters that feed on people. As the attacks grow worse, small things about her everyday life start to feel wrong. It suits readers who like moody, violent horror with a mystery underneath.
306: My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected @ Comic by Wataru Watari (Yen Press) is a sharp, wry school comedy with a romantic streak. Hachiman Hikigaya is a cynical loner who thinks high school friendship is a scam, so after he turns in an essay mocking youth, his teacher drafts him into the Service Club, run by the brilliant and icy Yukino Yukinoshita, to help other students with their problems. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy dry humor and awkward, honest characters.
307: I Got a Cheat Skill in Another World and Became Unrivaled in the Real World, Too by Miku (Yen Press) is a light, wish-fulfillment fantasy that moves between two worlds. Yuuya Tenjou is a bullied, lonely boy who moves into his late grandfather's house. There he finds a door to another world, and the strength he gains on the other side follows him back home. It's an easygoing read for fans of power-up stories with a feel-good streak.
308: Reborn to Master the Blade: From Hero-King to Extraordinary Squire by Hayaken (Yen Press) is an action fantasy light novel with a playful twist. After a lifetime of rule, the legendary Hero-King Inglis asks to be reborn so he can focus purely on fighting. He gets his wish but comes back as a girl, Inglis Eucus, in a world where a magic crest decides who may become a knight, and without one, she sets out to train as a squire instead. It suits fans of battle-hungry heroes and lively fights.
309: I May Be a Guild Receptionist, but I'll Solo Any Boss to Clock Out on Time by Mato Kousaka (Yen Press) is a breezy action comedy fantasy. Alina Clover took a receptionist job at the adventurers' guild because it promised a stable life and regular hours. When a tough dungeon boss threatens to keep her working overtime, she quietly takes care of it herself, and no one is supposed to know it was her. It's a fun read for anyone who has ever just wanted to go home on time.
314: Lonely Castle in the Mirror by Mizuki Tsujimura (Seven Seas), adapted from her novel, is a gentle, bittersweet fantasy drama. Kokoro has stopped going to school and spends her days shut in her room, until one day her mirror begins to glow and pulls her into a fairy-tale castle, where six other kids and a girl in a wolf mask are waiting. They're told a hidden key can grant one wish. It's a thoughtful read for anyone who likes quiet, emotional stories about feeling alone.
316: Kindergarten Wars by You Chiba (Yen Press) is a fast, funny action comedy. Black Lily is a kindergarten for the children of the rich and powerful, which makes it a favorite target for kidnappers and hitmen, so its teachers are all former assassins, hired to keep the kids safe at any cost. Rita is one of the best of them, and when she isn't fighting off attackers, she's hoping to find a boyfriend. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy over-the-top fights mixed with workplace comedy.
317: My Quiet Blacksmith Life in Another World by Tamamaru (J-Novel Club) is a cozy, low-stakes fantasy. A tired office worker gets a second chance at life in another world, along with a talent for crafting. He has no interest in being a hero, so instead he builds a forge deep in a forest and settles in to make knives and swords at his own pace. It suits readers who enjoy slow-life stories about craft, good company and simple days.
319: I'll Become a Villainess Who Goes Down in History by Izumi Okido (Yen Press) is a cheerful fantasy comedy. Alicia realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of a game she once played, and instead of trying to dodge her fate, she decides to embrace it and become the greatest villainess ever. The trouble is, her idea of being wicked keeps coming across as kind and clever. It's a fun, upbeat read for fans of villainess stories that turn the formula on its head.
322: The Water Magician by Tadashi Kubo (J-Novel Club) is an easygoing fantasy adventure light novel. After dying young, Ryo is reborn in a world of swords and magic with a gift for water magic and a body that doesn't age. All he wants is a peaceful, quiet life, so he starts out alone in the wilderness, slowly sharpening his magic, before heading out into the wider world. It suits readers who like thoughtful, steady fantasy with careful magic and a calm hero.
327: Is the Order a Rabbit? by Koi (Yen Press) is a sweet, gentle slice-of-life comedy. Cocoa Hoto moves to a pretty, old-fashioned town for high school and boards at the Rabbit House, a small coffee shop, where she meets Chino, the quiet granddaughter of the owner, and Tippy, the fluffy rabbit who rides on Chino's head. It's a calm, cozy read for anyone who enjoys cute characters and low stakes.
329: Phantom Thief Jeanne by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a sparkling magical girl adventure with plenty of comedy and romance. Maron Kusakabe seems like a normal high school girl, but she is the reincarnation of Joan of Arc, and with help from the angel-in-training Fin, she becomes the phantom thief Jeanne, stealing paintings where demons are hiding and sealing them away. A police detective's daughter, who happens to be her best friend, is determined to catch her. It's a classic for shojo fans who love magical girls.
331: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint by singNsong (Ize Press) is a gripping action fantasy light novel. Kim Dokja is an ordinary office worker and the only person who has read a long web novel about surviving the end of the world all the way through, and one night on the subway, the story comes true around him. Now his knowledge of every twist may be the only thing keeping him alive. It's a great pick for readers who love clever survival stories and big, layered worlds.
333: The Rose of Versailles by Riyoko Ikeda (Udon) is a sweeping historical drama and romance set in the years before the French Revolution. Oscar François de Jarjayes is raised as a son by her father so she can follow him into the military. She becomes the commander of the royal guard, protecting the young Marie Antoinette as she arrives in France, and court intrigue, friendship and love follow. It's a landmark shojo classic and a great fit for readers who enjoy history and big emotions.
334: Takahashi from the Bike Shop by Arare Matsumushi (Yen Press) is a warm, grounded romance about grown-ups. Pan Tokura is an office worker who has trouble saying no and is used to keeping her head down. When her bike breaks down, a blunt young man named Takahashi from the local bike shop fixes it, and little by little, the two get to know each other. It's a lovely pick for readers who like slow, realistic romance and characters learning to stand up for themselves.
336: Sword Art Online: Ordinal Scale by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is an action sci-fi story set in the world of Sword Art Online. A new device called the Augma has made augmented reality part of everyday life, and its hit game, Ordinal Scale, sends players out into the streets of Tokyo to battle monsters and climb the rankings. Kirito and Asuna join in, but something about the game soon seems off. It suits fans of the series and anyone who enjoys virtual-world action.
346: Ascendance of a Bookworm Part 3 by Miya Kazuki (J-Novel Club) continues a thoughtful fantasy about a girl who loves books more than anything. Urano, a book lover, was reborn as Myne in a world where books are rare treasures only nobles can afford. In Part 3, she takes a new name and steps into the world of the nobility, where she must learn its rules while still chasing her dream of making books for everyone. It's a rewarding read for fans of slow-building, detailed worlds.
349: Blend-S by Miyuki Nakayama (Yen Press) is a bright, silly workplace comedy. Maika Sakuranomiya is a sweet, cheerful girl who keeps losing part-time jobs because her natural expression looks like a scary glare. She's finally hired at Stile, a cafe where each waitress plays a character type, and Maika's assigned role is the sadist, which is the last thing she really is. It's an easy, fun read for anyone who likes quirky casts and gentle humor.
351: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Shadows by Sakaku Hishikawa (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy action story with a big heart. Zenos is a gifted healer who was kicked out of his adventuring party for not seeming useful enough, so with no license and few options, he opens a small clinic in the city's slums. His skill quickly draws a crowd of unusual patients, and word of him spreads. It suits readers who enjoy underdog heroes and stories about building a new place to belong.
360: Classroom of the Elite: Year 2 by Syougo Kinugasa (Seven Seas) is a tense psychological school drama light novel. At Advanced Nurturing High School, students are ranked, rewarded and punished through constant tests and competitions between classes. As Kiyotaka Ayanokoji, who prefers to stay in the background, begins his second year as a new group of first-years arrives, the contests get sharper and the rivalries more personal. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy mind games and schemes.
362: Reborn to Master the Blade: From Hero-King to Extraordinary Squire by Moto Kuromura (Yen Press) is an action fantasy manga with a playful twist. After a lifetime of rule, the legendary Hero-King Inglis asks to be reborn so he can focus purely on fighting. He gets his wish but comes back as a girl, Inglis Eucus, in a world where a magic crest decides who may become a knight, and without one, she sets out to train as a squire instead. It suits fans of battle-hungry heroes and lively fights.
366: Mobile Suit Gundam: Cucuruz Doan's Island by Junji Ohno (Vertical) is a sci-fi war story drawn from the original Mobile Suit Gundam. During the war between the Earth Federation and Zeon, young pilot Amuro Ray is sent to a remote island, where he meets Cucuruz Doan, a former Zeon soldier who now lives quietly, caring for a group of orphaned children. Amuro has to decide what this strange man really is. It's a thoughtful pick for Gundam fans who like the human side of the war.
370: Spriggan by Hiroshi Takashige (Seven Seas), with art by Ryoji Minagawa, is a fast, punchy action thriller. Long ago, a lost civilization left behind powerful relics, and the ARCAM Foundation works to keep them out of the wrong hands. Yu Ominae looks like an ordinary high school student, but he's one of ARCAM's top agents, called Spriggans, and each mission sends him around the world against armies and rival agents. It's a great pick for readers who love classic action and treasure-hunting adventure.
371: SSS-Class Revival Hunter by Bill K (Ize Press) is a dark, fast-moving action fantasy. In a world where hunters gain special skills, Kim Gong-ja feels left behind when his power turns out to be strange: it lets him come back from death and take on the skills of whoever killed him. It's a painful way to grow stronger, but it may be the only way he can rise. It suits readers who enjoy tower-climbing hunters and stories about a hero clawing his way up.
373: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale by Miri Mikawa (Yen Press) is a sweet fantasy romance. Anne Halford is a young girl who wants to become a silver sugar master, an artist who crafts beautiful sculptures from sugar. To reach the capital for a contest, she needs protection on the road, so she buys a proud, sharp-tongued fairy warrior named Challe as her bodyguard. It's a gentle read for anyone who enjoys craft, kindness and slow-burn romance.
374: Flower of Life by Fumi Yoshinaga (Tokyopop) is a funny, warm school comedy with real heart. Harutaro Hanazono starts high school a month late after recovering from leukemia, and he jumps right in, befriending the shy Shota and the prickly, manga-obsessed Majima. Together they deal with class projects, crushes and the strange ups and downs of being teenagers. It's a great fit for readers who like sharp humor, honest characters and everyday stories that sneak up on you emotionally.
381: Futari Escape by Shouichi Taguchi (Seven Seas) is a laid-back comedy about two women dodging grown-up life. One is a manga artist always behind on her deadlines, and the other is her easygoing friend who doesn't have a job. Whenever things get to be too much, the two run off together, chasing snacks, small trips and silly little adventures. It's a cozy, relaxing read for anyone who has ever wanted to escape their to-do list for a day.
398: Amazing Agent Luna by Nunzio DeFilippis (Seven Seas), co-written with Christina Weir and drawn by Shiei, is a fun action spy story. Luna is a teenage girl who was raised by the government to be the perfect secret agent. She can handle any mission, but her newest one is going undercover at an ordinary high school, where fighting bad guys is easy for her, but making friends and fitting in are a lot harder. It's a fun pick for readers who like spy action mixed with school comedy.
